proof:
# Coupled direction parameters for one actual residual pair

Use the d-dimensional simplex and compatible bodies A,B,K from
`candidate bad2020086fc16b6`,
with d>=2 and m=d+1. Choose actual P_j in R_j and P_l in R_l,
j!=l. No extremality among all points of A is assumed for these points.
Write E=[P_j,P_l] and b=vol_d(B), V=vol_d(T).

## 1. A single set of endpoint deficits determines both directions

For i outside {j,l} put

    a_i=-1-v_i.P_j>0,       b_i=-1-v_i.P_l>0.

Also put alpha=-1-v_l.P_j>0 and beta=-1-v_j.P_l>0. Since the
normals sum to zero, the heights above the opposite original cuts are

    H_j=1+v_j.P_j=m+alpha+sum a_i,
    H_l=1+v_l.P_l=m+beta+sum b_i.                    (1)

For Delta=P_j-P_l, define

    D_j=v_j.Delta=H_j+beta>m,
    D_l=-v_l.Delta=H_l+alpha>m.

The positive and negative normal increments have the same total M_0,
because sum_i v_i.Delta=0. Directly,

    M_0=sum_i(v_i.Delta)_+
       =m+alpha+beta+sum_(i outside {j,l})max(a_i,b_i). (2)

Normalize the two opposite directions by their own longitudinal normals:

    e_j=Delta/D_j,         e_l=-Delta/D_l.

Their sigma parameters from the sharp roof theorem are exactly

    sigma_j=M_0/D_j,       sigma_l=M_0/D_l.           (3)

Thus both are at least1. Both equal1 if and only if a_i=b_i for every
shared index i. Indeed M_0-D_j=sum_i(b_i-a_i)_+ and
M_0-D_l=sum_i(a_i-b_i)_+. No independent optimization of the two
directions is justified; they share all the data in(1)--(3).

## 2. Both sharp captured credits and a common missed credit are actual

Let q_j=vol_d(K intersect {v_j.x>=0}) and similarly q_l. Let
R_min(b;H,sigma) denote the exact direction-specific value proved in
Section6 of
`candidate 5e5b642b770e6623`,
with simplex volume V and dimension d fixed. Then

    2^d q_j>=R_min(b;H_j,sigma_j),
    2^d q_l>=R_min(b;H_l,sigma_l).                   (4)

To verify the hypotheses without silently replacing E by an extreme
segment of A, view E in the v_j coordinate: its lower endpoint is
-1-beta<-1 and its upper endpoint is H_j-1>d. Every B section has
longitudinal endpoints in[-d,1]. Thus every section of E+B straddles
0, and its captured length is exactly the upper B roof plus H_j-1.
The actual inclusion(E+B)/2 subset K proves the first inequality in(4).
The other direction is identical with the same segment reversed.

The additive normal-cone injection strengthens both inequalities to

    2^d q_j>=R_min(b;H_j,sigma_j)
                       +vol_d(A intersect {v_j.x>=d}),
    2^d q_l>=R_min(b;H_l,sigma_l)
                       +vol_d(A intersect {v_l.x>=d}). (5)

Here the relevant far tail plus B lies in the tested nonnegative cap,
because min_B v_j>=-d. The actual segment lies in an affine line,
which has zero d-volume. The injection in
`candidate 5fcdb1b3fadb0891` puts one
volume-preserving copy of the indicated tail outside that line+conv B,
disjoint from the whole E+B. This proof only requires E subset A,
not that its endpoints attain global A extrema. The two inequalities
in(5) are separate valid cap bounds; this note does not add their
injected sets or claim that they are mutually disjoint.

For the common missed set, put

    G=intersection_(i outside {j,l}){v_i.x<0},
    A_G=A intersect intersection_(i outside {j,l}){v_i.x<-1}.

The same actual segment, together with one disjoint injection of A_G,
gives the independently proved bound

    2^d vol_d(K intersect G)>2b+vol_d(A_G).          (6)

Equations(4)--(6) may therefore be imposed simultaneously with their
shared direction parameters. None of them replaces actual fiber sums
by integrals over an integer projection.

## Scope

There is no assertion that both sigma parameters must exceed1, nor that
the endpoint deficits have a uniform positive lower bound. The equality
condition in(3) is explicit. These are coupled actual-body necessary
inequalities, not a proof that every hypothetical bad critical circuit
violates one of them.
